title: Kinematics
summary: Wheel speeds to robot speeds, the WPILib way.

steps.title: Wheel speeds in, robot speeds out

say.never:
Last lesson you worked out the robot's speed with your own math. WPILib, the robot toolkit, has a class that does it for you: `DifferentialDriveKinematics`. You give it the two wheel speeds, and it gives back the robot's forward speed and turning speed together in a single object called `ChassisSpeeds`.

Say the left side does 3.0 m/s and the right side does 5.0 m/s. Kinematics works out that the robot moves forward at 4.0 m/s (the average) and turns at (5.0 - 3.0) / track width radians per second.
say.bit: `DifferentialDriveKinematics` does the math you wrote by hand last lesson: wheel speeds in, a `ChassisSpeeds` (forward and turning) out.

steps.title: In your lesson: Wheel speeds in, robot speeds out

say.never:
In `getChassisSpeeds()` you will do it in two moves. First bundle the two wheel speeds into one object, then hand it to kinematics:

`DifferentialDriveWheelSpeeds wheels = new DifferentialDriveWheelSpeeds(getLeftMetersPerSecond(), getRightMetersPerSecond());`

`return kinematics.toChassisSpeeds(wheels);`

The answer has `vxMetersPerSecond` (forward) and `omegaRadiansPerSecond` (turning).
say.bit: Bundle the two speeds as `new DifferentialDriveWheelSpeeds(left, right)`, then `kinematics.toChassisSpeeds(wheels)` returns forward (`vxMetersPerSecond`) and turning (`omegaRadiansPerSecond`).

Now let kinematics do the math. **Replace** the placeholder line `return new ChassisSpeeds();` with:

`return kinematics.toChassisSpeeds(wheels);`

Replace it rather than adding a second `return`. A method can only return once, and Java complains about code after a `return`.
say.bit: Replace `return new ChassisSpeeds();` with `return kinematics.toChassisSpeeds(wheels);`. Only one `return` allowed.
